A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same NHGD research work, with 41 pages and complete Appendices A–E. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable comparison of the methods, equations, proofs, figures and tables.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original experiments on MNIST hyper-data cleaning, Fashion-MNIST distillation and heat-equation-constrained optimization, including accuracy, loss and runtime results.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E retain the original experiments and reported outcomes for hyper-data cleaning, data distillation and PDE-constrained optimization.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices A and E retain the same NHGD updates, EFIM inverse approximation, cross-derivative estimators, parallel implementation and practical smoothing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST label cleaning, Fashion-MNIST distillation and the same 2D heat-equation control problem. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The experiment-specific comparator sets are unchanged, including Neumann/CG, stocBiO, AmIGO, TTSA and SOBA where reported, and Broyden for PDE optimization. Appendix E retains the same explanation of stocBiO's equivalence to Neumann for five-sample-per-class distillation.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E retain identical metrics and settings, including 50% MNIST label noise, distillation with 5 and 100 samples per class, batch sizes, iteration budgets, network architectures and PDE sampling procedures.

E4.justification: The existing comparisons across Neumann/CG truncation counts and distillation sample counts remain unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, error analysis or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Tables 2–5 retain identical plus/minus reporting and descriptions of averaging over the last 50 epochs. There are no changes to reported seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All experimental values, curves and reported findings in Section 5 and Appendix E are unchanged. For example, both report NHGD test accuracy of 0.9180 ± 0.0003 in Table 2 and PDE outer loss of 0.0266 ± 0.0005 in Table 5.

T1.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–D retain the same assumptions, Hessian–Fisher equivalence, approximation and convergence theorems, and proofs. No mathematical statement, bound or derivation changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about EFIM-based hypergradient approximation, parallel efficiency, sample complexity and empirical performance.

C2.justification: The result interpretations, Hessian–Fisher rationale and model-misspecification discussion in Remark 4.6 are unchanged. The conclusion retains the same future-work boundaries concerning single-loop algorithms and outer-variable-dependent data distributions.

D1.justification: Appendices A and E retain identical implementation details, hyperparameters, two-GPU A100 setup and code-source links. The new acknowledgment identifies support but adds no technical or resource-access information.

R1.justification: The same 41 cited works and research positioning are retained. Reference 34 corrects a malformed rendering of 'nystrom' in the existing title; this is a bibliographic correction, not a different citation or changed relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: v2 adds an Acknowledgment thanking the NVIDIA Academic Grant Program and UMN Data Science Initiative, corrects the malformed word in reference 34 and updates the version/date stamp. The scientific prose and appendix structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgment occupies the former start of the bibliography on page 13, moving References to page 14 and reflowing entries across pages 14–16. Figures, tables, captions and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 adds support attribution and repairs one malformed reference title, providing small editorial refinements. The methods, theory, empirical evidence, interpretations and reproducibility information remain identical, including the appendices; the localized edits do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
